The Care Requirements Checklist

What to confirm, write down and ask before you compare care arrangements for your wife.

Download PDF

The social worker has started saying “assisted living” and “memory care.” Before anyone compares one arrangement with another, make sure you have these in hand. Check what you've done. Anything unchecked is a job for the coming days, not a verdict about your wife or about you.

Write down

Confirm

Ask

What this checklist doesn't do

It helps you confirm, write down and ask. It doesn't say what a checked or an unchecked box means, what kind of care your wife needs, or which setting would suit her. Those belong to the people who assess her, and to the next step below.

Ready for the next step?

You know what to confirm, write down and ask. The care interview goes through your wife's daily life area by area, including the parts that don't show up at home, and turns your answers into a Family Care Profile you can bring to any care conversation.

Where this comes from

Items marked 1 follow the questions the Family Caregiver Alliance suggests families write answers to; the item marked 2 follows the National Institute on Aging's advice to consider the person's needs and wants. The rest come from the Family Care Roadmap's own working list for this step.

  1. Family Caregiver Alliance, Caregiving at Home: A Guide to Community Resources
  2. National Institute on Aging, How To Choose a Nursing Home or Other Long-Term Care Facility
